skill.name: generate-lut
skill.description: Generate creative .cube LUTs from photo color-grading requests, preview the exported LUT on a photo, and save a reusable recipe. Use for warm film looks, portraits, travel or street photography, LUT strength adjustments, batch photo grading, and LUT validation. Also supports explicitly specified technical color transforms, ordered LUT chains, and documented camera checks.
skill.summary: Create reproducible .cube color looks with exact-LUT previews, saved recipes, validation reports, and optional camera delivery checks.
skill.author: kaiyihe699-max

content.user_title: Generate Reusable Color LUTs With Photo Previews
content.value_statement: Color-grading ideas are difficult to reuse consistently across photos and editing tools. Generate deterministic .cube LUTs with exact-file previews, saved recipes, and validation reports.
actual_capabilities: Generate creative .cube LUTs from built-in presets or explicit contrast, saturation, warmth, exposure, curve, and RGB tint controls.
Package a final LUT with exact-file photo previews, a replayable recipe, SHA-256 checks, validation results, and a ZIP archive.
Blend normalized LUTs toward identity and apply a selected LUT to image folders while preserving source files.
Bake ordered normalized LUT chains and generate technical transforms with explicit source and target color settings.
Bake transforms from a user-supplied OpenColorIO configuration when PyOpenColorIO is installed.
Check LUT structure and documented camera-profile constraints, including Panasonic DC-S9 Photo Style tags and card filename rules.
limitations: The default creative workflow handles ordinary 8-bit sRGB photos, not RAW development, automatic Log detection, or HDR grading.
A single 3D LUT cannot encode grain, bloom, masks, or local adjustments, and cannot recover an exact reference-image grade.
Numerical checks and camera profiles do not certify visual quality, accurate film emulation, or successful import on a physical camera.
Photo previews require Python 3.10+ and Pillow with LittleCMS; the optional OCIO workflow also requires PyOpenColorIO and a supplied configuration.

best_practices: Confirm input encoding and destination settings before choosing a creative preset or technical transform.

Do not treat synthetic charts, numerical validation, or profile checks as proof of visual quality or real-camera compatibility.

faq.question: Does this skill need another AI API key?
faq.answer: No additional AI API key is required. Your agent interprets the request, and the Python image-processing scripts run locally.

faq.question: Can I try it without supplying a photo?
faq.answer: Yes. Use a bundled credited sample, or generate a package with synthetic charts when no input photo is supplied.

faq.question: How can I reproduce the same LUT?
faq.answer: Replay the saved recipe without overrides. Package generation regenerates the serialized recipe and checks that the LUT SHA-256 matches.

faq.question: Should I apply the exported creative LUT at full strength?
faq.answer: Yes, initially. Package strength is already baked into the LUT, and delivery previews apply that file at full strength.

faq.question: Can it process RAW, Log, or HDR automatically?
faq.answer: No. Develop RAW first and specify technical color assumptions separately. The default creative package expects ordinary 8-bit sRGB photos.

faq.question: Does a passing camera-profile check guarantee import?
faq.answer: No. It checks declared file and naming constraints. Test the LUT on the actual camera and review the resulting image.
